Across the Pacific, a different model of energy transition is rising 🌊
 
Not just a shift from diesel to renewables, but a whole-of-society transformation linking energy with mobility, food systems, digital infrastructure, and climate resilience.
 
In tourism-driven economies such as Fiji, Palau, Samoa, and Vanuatu, contributing 10% to 40% of GDP, renewable energy is already reducing operating costs and helping retain more value locally.
 
In French Polynesia, seawater air conditioning systems are cutting cooling electricity demand by up to 90%, showing how sustainable energy solutions can work with natural systems while improving efficiency.
 
At the 6th Pacific Regional Energy and Transport Ministers’ Meeting (PRETMM) in Port Moresby, I reflected on how this model is taking shape, not as a future vision, but as a system being built in real time.
 
🔹 Turning energy into a foundation for value chains: Electrification has increased from around 64% in 2009 to over 85% in 2022. The next frontier is what that energy enables. In Samoa, clean energy is expanding beyond electric vehicles to low-carbon outboard motors for fishing and sea transport, linking energy to livelihoods, markets, and mobility.
 
🔹 Building digital, data, and AI foundations: Energy systems need to be designed for both demand and risk. At UNDP, the SIDS Data Platform integrates over 4,000 indicators and 80+ geospatial datasets to support investment-ready, AI-enabled planning. In Tonga, a cable disruption in 2024 affected around one-third of the population for more than two weeks, highlighting the need for resilient, energy-backed digital systems. 
 
🔹 Shifting to distributed, resilient architectures: With urban centers growing at around 4% annually and geography limiting grid expansion, distributed systems are becoming central. In Papua New Guinea, where access remains around 20%, a 1 MW solar system in Bougainville is already delivering power to over 30,000 people, reducing costs by up to 50%. The new Off-Grid Regulation is now enabling these solutions to scale.
 
As the Pacific prepares to host pre-COP discussions ahead of COP31, there is a clear opportunity to bring this model to the global stage. 
 
Through Rising Up for SIDS and the SIDS Energy Offer, UNDP is working with partners to connect policy, finance, technology, and capacity into integrated systems that can scale.
 
If you are working in this space, we invite you to connect. We are ready to listen, partner, and support.
